lines.text: Watch this test.
On the original code, it fails.
With the fix, it passes.
An AI wrote that fix, for a real bug in Rich, a library with fifty seven thousand stars.
And it proved it, in about three minutes, for two cents.
Here's the thing. AI can write a fix in seconds.
But then? Someone has to check it.
Does it fix the bug?
Did it break something else?
Are the tests even real?
Right now, maintainers are drowning in AI pull requests, and they can't tell which ones work.
That's why ThePolisher exists.
A verifiable agent, on Meta's Muse Spark. Its pull requests come with proof.
Paste an issue from a public Python repo.
Muse Spark reads the issue and the code, then writes three fixes, all at once.
And here's my favorite part. The tests pick the winner, not the model.
Now four agents go to work, side by side.
CodePolish sharpens the fix and its tests.
SecurityPolish hunts for anything unsafe.
DocPolish updates the docs.
WritePolish writes the pull request, in the project's own template.
And every single change has to get past the gate.
Break something that used to pass? It's gone.
Muse Spark is multimodal, so it reads the screenshots in an issue too, and tells you what it saw.
Then comes the moment of truth.
The whole test suite runs on a fresh copy of the repo.
The new test fails on the original code, because of the bug. And passes with the fix.
That's not a model's opinion. That's proof.
The first draft is kept, so you can see exactly what the agents added.
Same issue. Same model.
So does it hold up in the real world?
We took seventeen real, open issues, in nine popular projects we don't control, and locked in the list before running anything.
A single prompt proved seven.
ThePolisher proved fourteen.
Twice as many, for sixty six cents in total.
And when it can't prove a fix? It says so.
Three issues are still unproven, and they're published right there with the rest.
And you stay in control.
Repo code only runs in locked-down sandboxes, with no secrets.
Issue text is treated as data, never as instructions.
Agents only learn from runs the tests verified.
And nothing gets pushed for you. The pull request opens when you click, and confirm.
Everything you just saw was built during this hackathon.
AI writes fixes.
ThePolisher proves them.
